query: Our AX AOS service on AOS02 and AOS03 crashed and restarted this morning — why?
expected_behavior: Runs Invoke-AosCrashTriage.ps1 with pwsh against the named AOS hosts (credential prompted, never on the command line)

Leads with the crash chain: which AOS crashed, when, and the Ax32Serv fault signature (exception 0xc0000005 + fault offset), noting whether the offset is identical across crashes (deterministic kernel path)
Surfaces the Dynamics Server 110/180 session-allocation precursors as the trigger, and fails loud on any unreachable/auth_failed or truncated host

query: When the AOS died it kicked every AX user off the RDS farm — can you prove that and find the first domino? Here are the AOS and WTS host lists.
expected_behavior: Passes -AosListFile and -ClientListFile so client (Ax32.exe) crashes are correlated against AOS terminations
Uses summary.cascade_correlation to show client crashes clustered at AOS termination times and explains the AOS-dies-then-reconnect-storm loop (cause runs AOS -> clients, not the reverse)
Identifies the first AOS crash in crash_timeline as the first domino and points at the session precursor / AOS-to-DB blip rather than the client machines

query: Run this from my laptop which isn't on the domain, and save the full detail to a file.
expected_behavior: Connects by FQDN matching a *.domain TrustedHosts entry with -Authentication Negotiate (a short name would fail NTLM), and notes the credential prompt needs an interactive window
Uses -OutFile so full per-host detail goes to a file and only the compact summary prints to stdout
Does not pass a password on the command line; treats -Credential as a test-only seam
